s1.syndrome_frame: Severe fatigue and muscular weakness with a large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger, associated with hypercalcemia, hypophosphatemia, and elevated parathyroid hormone levels
salient_findings: Large tumor on the distal part of the right fourth finger
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 60s
History of primary hyperparathyroidism 6 years prior to presentation
Patient refused therapeutic management for primary hyperparathyroidism
Patient is cachectic
Tumor on the right fourth finger has gradually enlarged in recent months
Hypercalcemia at 3.6 mmol/L
Hypophosphatemia at 0.65 mmol/L
Elevated serum parathyroid hormone at 380 pmol/L
Radiography showed complete lysis of the underlying phalanx and periosteal bone resorption
Chest radiograph revealed important deformation of the ribs
Thoracic CT scan revealed multiple lesions associated with multiple rib and vertebral fractures
Skull radiography showed pattern of trabecular resorption with 'salt-and-pepper' appearance

raw.champion: Primary hyperparathyroidism with osteitis fibrosa cystica and brown tumor
raw.rationale: The patient's history of primary hyperparathyroidism, refusal of therapeutic management, and current presentation of severe hypercalcemia, hypophosphatemia, and elevated parathyroid hormone levels, along with radiographic evidence of bone resorption and the presence of a brown tumor, best support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism
rejected.why: While the patient has a brown tumor, this option does not fully account for the underlying cause of hyperparathyroidism and its broader skeletal effects.

rejected.label: Osteitis fibrosa cystica
rejected.why: This is a complication of hyperparathyroidism but does not encompass the full spectrum of the patient's condition, including the primary cause and the brown tumor.

rejected.label: Parathyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: There is no direct evidence provided in the vignette to conclusively diagnose parathyroid carcinoma, such as a histopathological confirmation of the parathyroid gland tissue.

rejected.label: Hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome
rejected.why: This syndrome is a rare genetic disorder, and the vignette does not provide information on the patient's family history or genetic testing that would support this diagnosis.
